note: Adjudicated accidental variants (punctuation, orthography, capital accents). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero variants. Every ruling here repeats the one already recorded for the same place in the ministers' branch at ordinarium.confiteor, because the two editions punctuate the two confessions alike.

adjudicated.ruling: The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.
Comma before the vocative, with DO and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.confiteor w022, where the same edition omits the same comma, printing tibi pater.
No comma before the 'et' closing the series, with DO and with the corpus ruling at ordinarium.confiteor w028.
House rule (ORTHOGRAPHY.md): accents ARE printed on capitals. DO omits them on capitals throughout; handmissal-eo attests the practice, as at ordinarium.confiteor w038.
